accepted.match: "scale" defined differently in what-is-human-geography and maps-and-spatial-thinking
accepted.reason: Reviewed: genuine homonym. In What Is Human Geography, 'scale' means the scale of analysis (local → regional → global). In Maps and Spatial Thinking, 'scale' means map scale (the ratio between map distance and ground distance). Two standard, distinct geographic meanings of the word.

accepted.match: "territoriality" defined differently in political-geography and geopolitics
accepted.reason: Reviewed: compatible. Political Geography introduces territoriality as the general strategy of controlling area; Geopolitics applies it to power relations among states. Same concept, different emphasis; no contradiction.

accepted.match: "human development index (hdi)" defined differently in economic-development and human-development-indicators
accepted.reason: Reviewed: compatible at different depths. Economic Development names the HDI in passing as a broader-than-income measure; Human Development Indicators (owner) gives its full construction. Consistent meaning.

accepted.match: "node" defined differently in transportation and regional-geography
accepted.reason: Reviewed: genuine homonym across sub-fields. In Transportation a 'node' is a hub/terminal in a transport network; in Regional Geography a 'node' is the focal point organizing a functional (nodal) region. Different applications of the term.
